title: Find All The Lonely Nodes
statement:
You get `root`, the root of a non-empty binary tree. Call a node *lonely* when its parent has no other child: it is the parent's left child and the right child is missing, or the other way round. The root has no parent, so it is never lonely.

Return the values of all lonely nodes in the tree, in any order. If the tree has no lonely node, return an empty list.
notes:
## Intuition

Whether a node is lonely depends only on its parent: the parent must have exactly one child. So instead of asking each node "do I have a sibling?", which needs a link back to the parent, let every parent look at its own two children. A parent with exactly one child reports that child, and one walk over the tree finds them all.

A brute force could first record each node's parent and then count that parent's children, but the parent-side check needs no extra map.

## Approach

1. Keep a list `lonely` for the answer.
2. Run a recursive `visit` from `root`; an empty `node` returns at once.
3. If `node` has a left child but no right child, push the left child's value.
4. If it has a right child but no left child, push the right child's value.
5. Recurse into both children, then return `lonely` after the walk ends.

## Example 1, step by step

The tree is `[1,2,3,null,4]`: node 1 has children 2 and 3, and node 2 has only a right child, 4.

- At node 1 both children exist, so nothing is pushed.
- At node 2 the left side is empty and the right side holds 4, so `lonely` becomes `[4]`.
- Nodes 4 and 3 are leaves and add nothing.

The answer is `[4]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each node is visited once and does constant work.
- Space: O(h) for the recursion, where h is the tree height (up to n for a chain), plus the output.

## Pitfalls

- The root is never lonely, even when the tree has a single node; checking from the parent's side handles this naturally.
- A leaf is not lonely just because it has no children; loneliness is about siblings, not children.
- Push the child's value, not the parent's.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `lonely` | values of the lonely nodes found so far |
| `visit` | the recursive walk over the tree |
| `node` | the node currently being examined as a parent |

narration.2: Collect the values of lonely nodes here.
narration.4: Visit a node and check its own children.
narration.5: An empty spot has no children to check.
narration.6: Stop the walk on this branch.
narration.8: Only a left child: that child has no sibling.
narration.9: Record the lonely left child's value.
narration.11: Only a right child: that child has no sibling.
narration.12: Record the lonely right child's value.
narration.18: Start from the root, which itself can never be lonely.
narration.19: Every parent has been checked; return the collected values.
